overview: P10 gas is a mixture of 90% argon and 10% methane. It is the standard fill gas for gas-flow proportional counters, and is used in XRF spectrometers and radiation detectors. Sunrise Gases supplies P10 gas in 7 Cu.M. cylinders from Nagpur, open 24 hours a day.
about: P10 (also written P-10 or P 10) is 10% methane in 90% argon. The argon is ionised by radiation or X-rays, while the methane acts as a quenching gas: it absorbs stray ultraviolet photons and stabilises the discharge so the detector gives a stable, proportional signal.

P10 is most often used to supply the flow-proportional counter in wavelength-dispersive XRF spectrometers, and in alpha and beta particle counting systems, radiation monitors and some research detectors. Your instrument manual gives the flow rate and pressure it needs.

When you enquire, share the instrument model, required outlet pressure, quantity and whether you will exchange empty cylinders. Because P10 contains methane, use a regulator suitable for flammable-gas mixtures, ventilate the room and keep ignition sources away.

faq.question: What is P10 gas?
faq.answer: P10 gas is a calibration and detector gas made of 90% argon and 10% methane by volume. It is used mainly in gas-flow proportional counters, XRF spectrometers and radiation detection equipment.

faq.question: What is the composition of P10 gas?
faq.answer: P10 is 90% argon (Ar) and 10% methane (CH₄) by volume.

faq.question: Is P10 gas flammable?
faq.answer: Yes. P10 contains 10% methane and is normally supplied as a flammable gas mixture. Keep cylinders away from ignition sources, use it in ventilated areas and follow the Safety Data Sheet.

faq.question: What is P10 gas used for in XRF?
faq.answer: In wavelength-dispersive XRF spectrometers, P10 flows through the flow-proportional detector that counts X-rays, particularly from lighter elements.

faq.question: Is P10 the same as P-10 or P 10?
faq.answer: Yes. P10, P-10 and P 10 are different spellings of the same 90% argon, 10% methane mixture.
